nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, with coordinates indexed by a finite set of size $n$, and write $tP = \{t y : y \in P\}$. Then $P$ is reflexive when there is a lattice point $c$ in the interior of $P$ such that, for every integer $t \ge 1$, the lattice points in the interior of $tP$ are exactly the points $c + y$ with $y$ a lattice point of $(t-1)P$.

nodes.summary: Let $r = (r_1, r_2)$ and $x = (x_1, x_2)$ be pairs of positive integers with $r_1 < r_2$. Then $1 + \sum_{i=1}^{2} x_i (r_i \bmod r_j) = r_j$ holds for $j = 1, 2$ (the support form of the IDP necessary condition) if and only if either $r = (1, 1 + x_1)$ or $r = (1 + x_2, 1 + (1 + x_2)x_1)$.

The weighted projective space simplex $\Delta_{(1,q)}$ is reflexive and has the integer decomposition property if and only if $1 + \sum_{i=1}^{2} x_i (r_i \bmod r_j) = r_j$ for $j = 1, 2$.

nodes.title: Least common multiple of the weights $(2, 2, 3)$

nodes.summary: For a finite list $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ of natural numbers, $\operatorname{lcm}(q)$ is $\operatorname{lcm}(\cdots\operatorname{lcm}(\operatorname{lcm}(1, q_1), q_2)\cdots, q_n)$, the usual least common multiple of $q_1, \dots, q_n$; in particular the empty list has least common multiple $1$.
nodes.title: Least common multiple of a list of weights

nodes.summary: For a list $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ of natural numbers and $b \in \mathbb{N}$, the weight statistic is $w(q, b) = b - \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left\lfloor \frac{q_i b}{1 + q_1 + \cdots + q_n} \right\rfloor$.
nodes.title: The weight statistic

nodes.summary: Let $p = (p_1, \dots, p_m)$ and $w = (w_1, \dots, w_k)$ be lists of positive integers such that the weighted projective space simplices $\Delta_{(1,p)}$ and $\Delta_{(1,w)}$ are reflexive, and let $q = (p_1, \dots, p_m, (1 + \sum_i p_i) w_1, \dots, (1 + \sum_i p_i) w_k)$. Then $\Delta_{(1,q)}$ is reflexive.

nodes.title: The $h^*$-polynomial of a weighted projective space simplex

nodes.summary: For a list $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ of natural numbers, with coordinates indexed by the positions of the list, this is the convex hull in $\mathbb{R}^n$ of the standard basis vectors $e_1, \dots, e_n$ and the vector $-(q_1 e_1 + \dots + q_n e_n)$, whose $i$th coordinate is $-q_i$.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
